mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing F_AuthRequired removes the only constraint forcing unauthenticated requests to the Unauthenticated outcome; the injection then constructs an Operation with no caller but Success outcome, which directly violates the AuthRequired predicates.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuthBypass { some op: Operation | no op.opCaller and op.opOutcome = Success }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing F_NonMemberIsNotFound lets a caller succeed on an op against a team they are not a member of; the injection asserts such an instance exists, breaking LeastPrivilege and FR_004_CallerIsMember which require every successful op to come from a real team member.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_NonMemberSuccess { some op: Operation | op.opOutcome = Success and (no m: Membership | m.mUser = op.opCaller and m.mTeam = op.opTeam) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing F_CrossTeamIsolation removes the rule that cross-team task access must return NotFound; the injection forces an Operation whose task belongs to a different team than the caller's X-Team-Id yet still succeeds, which is exactly the FR-014 leakage we want to forbid.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CrossTeam { some op: Operation | some op.opTask and some op.opTeam and op.opTask.tTeam != op.opTeam and op.opOutcome = Success }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing F_OwnerOrAdminForMutation removes the only constraint that ties successful PATCH/DELETE to ownership-or-admin; the injection constructs a non-owner non-admin member successfully editing a task, the canonical FR-009 violation.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_NonOwnerEdit { some op: Operation | op.opKind = EditTask and op.opOutcome = Success and some op.opTask and op.opCaller != op.opTask.tOwner and (no m: Membership | m.mUser = op.opCaller and m.mTeam = op.opTeam and m.mRole = AdminRole) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing F_AppendOnlyOneSource removes the structural one-producer-per-entry constraint; the injection forces two distinct operations to share a single AuditEntry, which is exactly the rewrite/duplicate scenario FR-016's append-only invariant forbids.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_DupAuditSource { some disj op1, op2: Operation | some ae: AuditEntry | op1.opAudit = ae and op2.opAudit = ae }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing F_AttributionCorrectness lets the audit entry's recorded actor diverge from the operation's actual caller; the injection forces such a misattribution, the canonical FR-015 violation.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_Misattribution { some op: Operation | some op.opAudit and op.opAudit.aActor != op.opCaller }
